# Hook type

**What kind of first line or first image is it?** · [all approaches](index.md) · clashes: C15, C35


## Contrarian take / 'Don't buy X'
<a id="contrarian-take"></a>

Open with something most people believe and say it is wrong, or tell them not to buy or do the obvious thing.

**Looks like:** 'Don't buy the RTX 5070 at ₹2 lakh.' The price is on screen and a red DON'T BUY stamp lands on the box in the first second. The rest gives the better alternative.

**Good at:** comments and debate; reach; positions you as an expert; saves when an alternative follows

**Weak at:** needs real evidence; pure debunks can leave the viewer with nothing (Rahul's weakest reel)

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long · niches all · goals comments, reach, trust · effort low

**How:** Say the take in the first line. Add a stamp or strike-through graphic in CapCut, or a HyperFrames stamp card.

**Backed by:** [Contrarian statement or "don't buy X"](../topics/hooks.md#hook-contrarian-statement), [Strong take, then defend or teach](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-strong-take), [Industry trope, then your contrary view](../topics/story.md#story-industry-contrarian), [Warning hook: never start X without these N things](../topics/hooks.md#l11-warning-hook), [Price strikes, stamps, pills and ticks](../topics/effects.md#fx-price-strike-through) · sources L05, R1, L06

## Curiosity question or 'do this now'
<a id="curiosity-question"></a>

Ask about a pain the viewer has, or give them a tiny action to try while watching.

**Looks like:** 'Does your animation look robotic?' over a robot-vs-pro side-by-side. Or 'Put your phone on airplane mode right now...' while the code keeps changing on screen. The answer is held back until the middle.

**Good at:** retention through an open loop; saves on practical tips; universal reach with everyday topics

**Weak at:** questions can sound generic; the payoff must be worth the wait

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, yt-short · niches all · goals retention, saves, reach · effort low

**How:** Put the question as text on frame 1 with the spoken line. For 'do this now', show the exact steps in a screen recording.

**Backed by:** [Question on a pain point](../topics/hooks.md#hook-pain-question), ["Do this now": a tiny effort, instant payoff](../topics/hooks.md#hook-do-this-now), ["You've probably seen X lately…"](../topics/hooks.md#hook-trend-riding), [Open loops, re-open one at ~15 s](../topics/story.md#story-open-loops), [Desire hook: this is exactly what you want to see](../topics/hooks.md#l11-desire-hook) · sources L02, L03, L05, R1, L04

## Contrast: looks X, sounds Y / before vs after
<a id="contrast"></a>

Two things side by side, or a two-part line that sets up the problem in one glance.

**Looks like:** Top text: 'Looks pro.' Then: 'Sounds like this: 🔇' over a silent clip. Or a split screen: wrong form left, right form right. The viewer gets the gap before a word of explanation.

**Good at:** instant clarity; works muted; saves (wrong vs right); easy to make visual

**Weak at:** needs a clean visual difference; overused before/afters feel stale

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, yt-short, carousel · niches all · goals retention, saves, shares · effort low

**How:** Split-screen layout in CapCut/Edits, or two text lines that pop in sequence with a pop SFX.

**Backed by:** [Contrast hook: looks X, sounds Y](../topics/hooks.md#hook-contrast-looks-sounds), [Conflict and a shared enemy](../topics/story.md#story-conflict-everywhere), [Gym: wrong vs right split-screen tip](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-gym-wrong-vs-right), [Untangle: hook, format, topic, illustration](../topics/growth.md#growth-untangle-data), [Desire hook: this is exactly what you want to see](../topics/hooks.md#l11-desire-hook) · sources L02, L03, L09, SP

## Proof or verdict first
<a id="proof-first"></a>

The result, number or verdict comes in the first second, with no intro.

**Looks like:** 'Core i9 14900K. ₹46,000. 3 out of 10.' The product card, price and score pop in one after another in the first second. Or a myth quoted as text while the lift that disproves it is already moving.

**Good at:** no wasted seconds; trust; short proof reels (6–18 s); clear covers

**Weak at:** gives the answer away early, so the body needs its own pull; needs real proof on hand

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, yt-short · niches all · goals retention, trust, reach · effort low

**How:** Start the edit on the proof frame. Add the number card or score in CapCut, or as a HyperFrames counter.

**Backed by:** [Verdict first: name, price, score](../topics/hooks.md#hook-verdict-first), [No intro: topic and number first](../topics/hooks.md#hook-no-intro-payoff-first), [Claim plus instant visual proof](../topics/hooks.md#hook-bold-claim-visual-proof), ["8 Mile": disprove the counter-argument first](../topics/story.md#story-8-mile), [70 / 20 / 10 proven, iterate, experiment](../topics/growth.md#growth-70-20-10) · sources R1, L01, SP, research

## Undercut a paid offer
<a id="undercut"></a>

Play or quote a rival's strongest line, then undercut it: 'He sells this for $97. I'm giving it away free.'

**Looks like:** A rival's clip plays in a card: 'I didn't edit a single second of this video.' A $97 checkout card pops onto it. Cut to you: 'I'm giving it away for free.' Every step is then explained.

**Good at:** comments; perceived value; trust when you really deliver

**Weak at:** uses someone else's content (originality risk); can look petty; needs a real paid rival

**Best for:** formats reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches tech, gym · goals comments, follows, trust · effort medium

**How:** Rival clip in a rounded card (CapCut overlay or HyperFrames), a price card on the word, then your face full frame.

**Backed by:** [Undercut a paid course in the hook](../topics/hooks.md#l10-undercut-paid-hook), [Pause-and-play breakdown of a reel](../topics/ideas.md#l10-pause-and-play-breakdown), [Teaching format: template card, then a real example](../topics/editing.md#l11-template-then-example), [Comment KEYWORD and I'll send it](../topics/growth.md#growth-comment-keyword-cta), [Sponsor as the "pro" answer](../topics/business.md#biz-sponsor-as-smart-option) · sources L10

## Expertise hook: years of X in 60 seconds
<a id="expertise-compression"></a>

Template '[N years] of [niche] in [60 seconds]'. Authority plus time compression in one line: my years, your minute.

**Looks like:** Frame 1: Srijan at the rack, text '4 SAAL KA GYM TRAUMA / 60 SECONDS' while he says it. A fast blitz of the mistakes follows, one per cut. Adam's example: '3 years of therapy in 60 seconds' (40.5M).

**Good at:** context and lean in one line; authority without bragging; sets up a fast list body; works in any niche

**Weak at:** needs real years behind it; the body must actually feel condensed; big promise (C7)

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, yt-short · niches all · goals retention, follows, saves · effort low

**How:** Say it in the first second with the number and niche as on-screen text. Cut the body as a blitz (one lesson per 2–3 s) with n/5 badges in CapCut or HyperFrames.

**Backed by:** [Expertise hook: years of niche in 60 seconds](../topics/hooks.md#l11-expertise-hook), [Hook template bank (fill in the blanks)](../topics/hooks.md#l11-hook-template-bank), [Hook window: 2–3 s short, 15–20 s long](../topics/hooks.md#hook-window-short-vs-long), [Untangle: hook, format, topic, illustration](../topics/growth.md#growth-untangle-data) · sources L11

## Warning hook: never start X without these N things
<a id="warning-gate"></a>

Template 'Never start a [X] if you don't have these [Y] things'. A prohibition on a big step, gated by a counted checklist the viewer checks themselves against.

**Looks like:** 'Never build a gaming PC if you don't have these 4 things.' Four number tiles pop in (1-2-3-4) and a red '4 THINGS' lands. Each item gets one shot and one reason. Adam's example: 'Never start a business if you don't have these 4 things' (339K).

**Good at:** loss aversion; open loop (which things? do I have them?); saves; ends with something useful, unlike a pure debunk

**Weak at:** preachy if the items are generic; needs 3–4 items that are really needed; list fatigue (C3/C20)

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, carousel · niches all · goals saves, retention, comments · effort low

**How:** Number tiles or n/4 badges in CapCut or HyperFrames, a hit SFX on the count word. Keep each item to one line plus a reason.

**Backed by:** [Warning hook: never start X without these N things](../topics/hooks.md#l11-warning-hook), [Contrarian statement or "don't buy X"](../topics/hooks.md#hook-contrarian-statement), [Promise a numbered list or a download](../topics/story.md#story-promised-list-open-loop), [Promise hook: daily habit, three payoffs](../topics/hooks.md#l11-promise-hook), [Anti-CTA: no DM needed, it's all here](../topics/growth.md#growth-anti-cta) · sources L11

## Desire hook: this is exactly what you want to see
<a id="desire-what-good-looks-like"></a>

Template 'This is exactly what you want to see when you're [situation]'. 'This' points at the ideal outcome on screen; the situation lets the right viewer self-select.

**Looks like:** Frame 1 is the proof: a spotless second-hand GPU with the warranty seal intact, temps 62°C. Voice: 'This is exactly what you wanna see jab tum second-hand GPU kholte ho.' Adam's example: an aerial warehouse with a map pin, 'when you're buying an industrial property' (3.6M).

**Good at:** shows what good looks like; self-selecting audience; saves; visual proof does the work

**Weak at:** spoken context lands last (C35); useless without a strong visual; needs the real thing to film

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, yt-short · niches all · goals saves, trust, retention · effort medium

**How:** Open on the proof shot, not your face. Put the situation as text on frame 1 so the context isn't late. A funny snapback line can follow ('…aur mummy bolti hai kuch fark nahi pada').

**Backed by:** [Desire hook: this is exactly what you want to see](../topics/hooks.md#l11-desire-hook), [Claim plus instant visual proof](../topics/hooks.md#hook-bold-claim-visual-proof), [Teaching format: template card, then a real example](../topics/editing.md#l11-template-then-example), [Contrast hook: looks X, sounds Y](../topics/hooks.md#hook-contrast-looks-sounds) · sources L11

## Promise hook: daily habit, three payoffs
<a id="promise-habit-payoff"></a>

Template 'If you [do B] every single day, you're going to [X], [Y] and [Z]'. A tiny repeatable habit with three stacked, concrete outcomes.

**Looks like:** Srijan scoops creatine or laces up for a walk; the three payoffs pop as text one by one on the beat, the third one is the joke ('…aur Sunday ki biryani guilt-free'). Adam's example: creatine, 'build more muscle, recover faster…' (28M, the biggest in the reel).

**Good at:** low cost, high payoff framing; rule of three rhythm; catches several motives at once; gym and habit content

**Weak at:** overpromising (C7); health claims need to be true; generic if the habit is obvious

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, yt-short · niches gym, tech, gaming · goals saves, shares, retention · effort low

**How:** Write three payoffs that are concrete and true. Pop each as text with a pop SFX in CapCut/Edits, or HyperFrames kinetic text.

**Backed by:** [Promise hook: daily habit, three payoffs](../topics/hooks.md#l11-promise-hook), [Lean: proof, pain/benefit or shock](../topics/hooks.md#hook-lean-three-ways), [Triple hook: context, lean, snapback](../topics/hooks.md#hook-triple-hook-formula), [Hook template bank (fill in the blanks)](../topics/hooks.md#l11-hook-template-bank), [Hook, problem, journey, lesson, CTA](../topics/story.md#story-hook-problem-journey-lesson-cta) · sources L11

## Mixing
Any of these can sit in the 'lean' slot of a triple hook. Proof-first plus contrarian ('3/10, don't buy') is Rahul's usual pairing. Contrast is the visual form of a contrarian take. L11's four templates slot into a triple hook: Expertise and Promise are context + lean in one line; Warning is a contrarian take that opens a checklist; Desire needs a proof visual from frame 1.

## Rule of thumb
Debate and comments: contrarian. Saves on how-tos: curiosity or contrast. Ratings and proof reels: proof-first. Free alternatives to paid things: undercut. Authority and a fast list body: expertise. Saves on a big decision: warning. Proof footage of the ideal result: desire. Habits and gym: promise.
